summary: Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1928–1931) and held posts at Ryukoku University (~1962–1975) and Kansai University.
Kavita Singh (1964–2023) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (~1982–1985) and Panjab University (~1985–1987).

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as headmaster at Maharaja's Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and taught at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1922), teaching Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz and Herbert Bruce Hannah.
Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1953) and was professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1995–2017).

Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Tokushima University (~1978–1991) and served as professor emeritus at Rikkyo University (attested 2015–2019).

Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and taught Shinshu Kusumoto. He held posts as assistant professor (attested 1982–1988) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013) at Shuchiin University.

Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) studied at Nagoya University (~1978–1982), Hokkaido University (~1982–1985), and Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1985–1988). He served as professor of geography at Kyoto University's Graduate School of Letters (~2009–2024).

Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Sophia University, Kyoto University, and Cornell University under Jay Jasanoff. He held posts at Nagoya City University (~1989–1995) and as professor at Kyoto University (~1995–2020).

Kazuhiro Furuta (born 1940) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was affiliated with the Otani Society as editor and publisher (attested 1991) and served as dean at Otani University (attested 1998).
Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) focuses on Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at Koyasan University (~2000–2005) and served there as a researcher (attested 2005).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Silpakorn University under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).

Kazunobu Matsuda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, where he later lectured (attested 1985–1989), and taught Shintaro Kitano and Ikko Arai. He held posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and the Eastern Institute.

Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe. He served as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1983–2014) and served on the Otani Society committee.

Kazuo Kano (born 1974) studied at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Klaus-Dieter Mathes. He held posts at Hamburg, Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Komazawa University.
Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1954–1963), where he later served as a professor (~1976–2005) and taught Jamie Hubbard.

Kazuo Osumi (1932–2024) worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955) and held posts at Hokkaido University (~1973–1985) and Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1985–2003).
Kazuo Oyamada (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tamagawa University (~1971–1975) and held a post at Rissho University (~1995).

Kazuyoshi Hotta works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo and served the University of Tokyo Young Buddhist Association (attested 2007), later holding a term-limited assistant professorship at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shudo Junior & Senior High School and the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948), holding posts at Hosen Gakuen College (~1965–1985) and Shogen Junior College.
Kazuyoshi Soma (born 1942) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Meiji Yamada and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
